s.h: KEY ESSENTIALS TO BEHAVIOR MANAGEMENT CORP
s.t:
BCBA — Remote Program Manager
Fully Remote · Telehealth Clinical Leadership
Role
BCBA — Remote Program Manager
$90,000 – $110,000/year (Exempt, Salaried)

$50 – $60/hr
Employment Type
Full-time and Part-time positions available · Fully Remote
Reports To
Clinical Director (Jazmin) with Chief Clinical Director (Maritza) oversight
Location
Fully Remote — Georgia residency preferred for state licensure alignment
Service Setting
100% Telehealth — virtual clinical delivery, virtual supervision, virtual team leadership
Core Hours
2:00 PM – 7:00 PM PST, minimum 5 hours visible presence (camera on)
Billable Split
70% direct billable · 30% indirect billable
Credential
Active BCBA Certification · Master's required · 3+ years post-cert experience · State licensure current · Reliable high-speed internet and professional remote workspace required
Why This Role Exists
Most remote BCBA jobs are thin wrappers around case management — you read reports, sign off on treatment plans from a couch, and rarely touch actual clinical supervision. KEBM built the Remote Program Manager role differently.

You lead a team of BCBAs and behavior technicians via telehealth, carry a real billable caseload at a 70/30 direct-to-indirect split, and own program quality across virtual service delivery. This is clinical leadership for BCBAs who want remote flexibility without giving up real authority.

If you have the discipline to run a clinical operation without a physical office to walk into — and the professional setup to do it well — this is structured for you.

We're a five-clinic ABA therapy company with four locations across Southern California and one in Georgia, founded in 2016 by a BCBA with 25+ years in the field. Our team of 68+ professionals delivers evidence-based therapy through our proprietary S.O.C.I.A.L. P.O.D.S. methodology — and our Sensory Spot locations prove that therapy can actually feel like play.
We serve every client who walks through our doors — insurance-funded, private pay, open play, and camp families alike. We're women-founded, minority-owned, and we don't sacrifice clinical quality for profit. If you want to work somewhere that's serious about outcomes and serious about its people, you're in the right place.
How S.O.C.I.A.L. P.O.D.S. Work
S.O.C.I.A.L. P.O.D.S. is our proprietary pod-based group ABA model. Clients are grouped 3–6 per pod at a 1:3 facilitator ratio, with a supervisor always on-site and clinical support always available in every pod. We use a push-in / pull-out model for group and 1:1 work, and BCBAs provide real-time clinical oversight across pods.

As the Remote Program Manager, your role is to extend clinical leadership, supervision, and program quality to the virtual team — coaching BCBAs and behavior technicians who deliver services through telehealth, managing cases that are better served virtually, and ensuring the S.O.C.I.A.L.

P.O.D.S. methodology translates with fidelity to remote delivery.
Who We Serve
KEBM serves every client who walks through our doors — no tiers, no priority treatment, no "real clients vs. drop-ins." That means:
Insurance-funded ABA clients (Medi-Cal, Medicare, commercial insurance)
Private pay therapy clients
Open play participants at our Sensory Spot locations
Camp participants — spring break, winter break, summer, and any seasonal KEBM camp
Consultation clients in adult residential and group home settings
Telehealth clients — the population you'll serve directly as Remote Program Manager
A camp kid gets the same quality of care as an insurance client. A telehealth client gets the same quality of care as a clinic-based client. If that feels natural to you, you're going to fit here. If the idea of treating any of those clients as less-than bothers you, this isn't the place.

Lead and supervise a team of BCBA clinicians and behavior technicians remotely — virtual supervision sessions, team meetings, performance evaluations, and real-time coaching. You're running a clinical operation through a camera.
Carry a direct billable caseload (70% of your time) — FBAs, treatment plan authorship, progress monitoring, and clinical decision-making on your assigned cases via telehealth.
Own program quality across virtual service delivery — quality assurance processes, treatment fidelity monitoring, outcome measurement, and continuous improvement of KEBM's telehealth program.
Manage virtual crisis situations and escalations — remote emergency support, crisis protocol implementation, coordination with on-site teams when a client situation escalates beyond telehealth scope.
Ensure telehealth compliance end-to-end — HIPAA in remote operations, state-specific telehealth regulations, privacy protocols, and documentation standards for virtual service delivery.
Develop virtual training programs and drive staff competency — onboarding, ongoing professional development, telehealth service delivery protocols, and technical support for the virtual team.
Generate program data and reports — utilization metrics, outcome tracking, program presentations for the CD and CCD. Telehealth programs live or die by data — this is yours to own.
Maintain core presence hours (2:00 PM – 7:00 PM PST) with camera on — visible, available, responsive. This is not optional; it's the structural commitment remote clinical leadership requires.

s.h: In your first 90 days, success looks like
s.t: Full remote team integration established, caseload at 70/30 billable/indirect cadence, quality assurance baseline documented across telehealth service delivery, and first monthly program report delivered to the CD.

s.h: You might be perfect for this if
s.t:
You hold your BCBA with leadership experience — and you genuinely thrive working remotely. This is not a "I'll figure it out" role. The BCBAs who succeed here already know they work well in virtual environments.
You want clinical authority without the commute — and you're willing to show up for it. Remote clinical leadership requires MORE presence, not less — cameras on, visible availability, responsive communication.
You have the setup — professional remote workspace, reliable high-speed internet, proper lighting and audio, and the discipline to hold core hours. KEBM provides platforms; you provide the operating environment.
You read remote work as a medium, not an excuse — you understand that virtual clinical supervision is harder than in-person supervision, not easier. If you were looking for a remote BCBA job because you wanted less accountability, this isn't it.

5+ years post-BCBA clinical experience
Prior telehealth ABA service delivery experience
Multi-state licensure (CA + GA or additional states)
Bilingual (Spanish)
Experience developing or scaling virtual clinical programs

These are non-negotiable for a fully remote clinical leadership role. If you can't commit to every one of them, this isn't the right role for you.
Professional workspace — dedicated office space or room with a door that can close for client confidentiality and professional appearance on camera.
Reliable high-speed internet — sufficient bandwidth for video supervision without dropouts. Minimum 25 Mbps up/down recommended; hardwired connection preferred over Wi-Fi.

## Company Description ##
**About Syngenta**
At Syngenta Crop Protection, we're pioneering solutions that safeguard global food security while championing sustainable agriculture. As a world market leader headquartered in Switzerland, we empower farmers with innovative crop protection technologies that defend against nature's toughest challenges.

We unite advanced science with digital solutions to develop intelligent crop protection that maximizes yields while minimizing environmental impact.

Join our mission of revolutionizing plant protection from seed to harvest. **Syngenta has been ranked as a-top employer-by Science Magazine and it has been awarded with the "Friendly Work Space" label to all its Swiss sites.**
## Job Description ##
At Syngenta, our goal is to build the most collaborative and trustworthy team in agriculture, providing top-quality seeds and innovative crop protection solutions that improve farmers' success. To support this mission, we are seeking a **Global Environmental Technology Lead**. This is a hybrid role based primarily in Muttenz, Switzerland, though Monthey can also be considered.
As Global Environmental Technology Lead, you will shape how Production & Supply identifies, develops and deploys the technologies that reduce environmental impact while protecting operational performance and our license to operate.

This is a high-impact global role for an accomplished scientist or engineer who can move confidently between technical depth, strategic direction and practical implementation. You will connect manufacturing sites, process development, environmental specialists and external partners to turn complex environmental challenges into scalable solutions.

* Set the global environmental technology strategy across waste, wastewater, air emissions, vent treatment, recovery and recycling, informed by Best Available Techniques (BAT).
* Identify, assess and mature emerging technologies, taking opportunities from laboratory and pilot-scale evidence through to robust manufacturing application.
* Partner with global and local manufacturing teams to solve critical environmental challenges, improve site performance and safeguard license to operate.
* Provide technical leadership and independent challenge for environmental projects, assessing feasibility, environmental benefit, risk, operability and cost.
* Influence product and process choices early by evaluating waste streams, especially wastewater, during active-ingredient process development.
* Develop practical, high-value solutions that reduce impacts to air, water and land across existing products and manufacturing sites.
* Build and lead a connected global environmental technology community spanning Technology & Engineering, Production & Supply, Environmental Managers, process development teams and external experts.
* Grow internal capabilities through technical coaching, knowledge exchange, training, literature reviews and partnerships with suppliers, consultants and technology providers.
* Translate complex environmental science and regulation into clear choices and decisive action for technical and business stakeholders.

* Master-s degree, or equivalent, in Chemistry, Chemical Process Engineering or a related discipline.
* Ideally 10+ years- experience in industrial chemical operations and/or process development.
* Demonstrated expertise in environmental technologies and a practical understanding of environmental legislation.
* Able to remain focused, resilient and effective in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment.
* Strong knowledge of waste, wastewater, emissions, recovery and recycling technologies.
* Solid grounding in organic and inorganic chemistry, chemical processes and process engineering; agrochemical production knowledge is an advantage.
* Working knowledge of environmental toxicity, chemical bio-transformation and environmental risk assessment.
* Proven ability to lead teams or workstreams in project, departmental or matrix environments.
* Experience in project and change management, with resilience in ambiguous environments.
* Strong analytical, conceptual, organisational and negotiation skills.
* Clear communication and stakeholder-influencing skills at all levels.
* Experience working across multicultural, multinational teams, with a recognised record of technical delivery.
* Fluent business English; French is highly advantageous.

Täglich fahren Millionen Autos durch Deutschland, und in den meisten bleibt Platz ungenutzt. Wir ändern das.
MUVN ist ein digitaler Transportmarktplatz. Wir bringen Fahrer:innen mit freiem Laderaum mit Menschen und Unternehmen zusammen, die etwas transportieren müssen. Günstiger, versichert, ohne Umweg.
Wir bauen gerade an mehreren Dingen gleichzeitig: einem neuen Produkt für gewerbliche Versender, Piloten mit großen Marken, neuen Strecken, Integrationen. An jedem dieser Themen arbeiten mehrere Menschen aus mehreren Bereichen, und keiner von ihnen hat den vollen Überblick über alle anderen.
Genau dafür gibt es diese Stelle. Du weißt zu jeder Zeit, wo jedes Projekt steht, was als Nächstes ansteht und wo es gerade klemmt. Eine Frage zum aktuellen Sprint, und du kannst sie beantworten. Eine Frage zu einem Partnerprojekt, und du gehst auf die Leute zu und sorgst dafür, dass am Tag X alles steht.
Du bist kein Product Owner und musst nicht entwickeln können. Du musst verstehen, worum es geht, grob einschätzen können, was etwas bedeutet, und Dinge über die Ziellinie bringen.
Hierfür suchen wir dich ab dem 01.10.2026 als Verstärkung für unser Team in Hamburg 🚀
Aufgaben
Überblick über alle Projekte
Du führst die Timeline über Marktplatz, unser Produkt für gewerbliche Versender, Integrationen und Partnerprojekte. Status, nächster Meilenstein, offene Entscheidungen, Risiken. Alles an einem Ort, aktuell, und für jeden im Team in zwei Minuten auffindbar.
Themen aktiv vorantreiben
Du wartest nicht auf Statusmeldungen, du holst sie dir. Freundlich und hartnäckig, bis erledigt wirklich erledigt heißt.
Abhängigkeiten und Termine
Du erkennst früh, wo sich Themen gegenseitig blockieren, über Tech, Marketing, Operations und externe Partner hinweg. Und du eskalierst konkret: nicht "das wird knapp", sondern "wenn X bis Freitag nicht steht, verschiebt sich Y um zwei Wochen".
Launches und Piloten
Du planst und begleitest den Start neuer Produkte, Features und Partnerprojekte. Wer liefert was bis wann, was muss am Tag X stehen, was lernen wir danach. Und du baust Checklisten, die beim zweiten Mal besser funktionieren als beim ersten.
Schnittstelle zu Tech
Wir sind ein technisches Produkt, deshalb hängt vieles an unserem CTO. Du bist die Schnittstelle zwischen ihm und den laufenden Projekten. Du verstehst genug vom Thema, um in einem Kunden- oder Partnergespräch grob einzuschätzen, was etwas bedeutet, und um die richtige Rückfrage zu stellen.
Ziele und Rhythmus
Du hältst den Takt: Zyklen, Check-ins, Reviews, sichtbarer Fortschritt. Die Ziele setzen die Gründer:innen und die Verantwortlichen. Dass sie nachgehalten werden, liegt bei dir.
Meetings und Entscheidungen
Für deine projektübergreifenden Runden bereitest du vor und nach: Agenda, Unterlagen, Ergebnisse, To-dos mit Verantwortlichem und Datum. Entscheidungen dokumentierst du so, dass sie zwei Wochen später nicht neu verhandelt werden.
Externe Partner
Agenturen, Pilotpartner, Dienstleister. Du steuerst die Zusammenarbeit: Lieferungen, Termine, Feedbackschleifen.
Prozesse und KI
Wiederkehrendes standardisierst du mit Vorlagen und Checklisten. Du arbeitest KI-first: Statusberichte, Protokolle, Recherche und Dokumentation baust du mit KI. Was dabei rauskommt, prüfst du. Die Richtigkeit gehört dir, nicht dem Tool.
Qualifikation
Du hast mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung im Projekt- oder Programmmanagement, gerne in einem Startup, einer Agentur oder einem digitalen Produktumfeld. Du hast schon einmal ein Projekt mit mehreren Beteiligten und einem harten Termin über die Ziellinie gebracht, ohne selbst die fachliche Arbeit gemacht zu haben.
Du bist nah dran an digitalen Produkten. Tiefe Technikkenntnisse brauchst du nicht, aber du musst Sachzusammenhänge verstehen und grob einschätzen können, was ein Wunsch bedeutet, bevor du ihn zusagst.

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Every contact that reaches a customer support agent, and every credit issued to customers, represents a defect somewhere in our system. This role exists to help find those defects, trace them to their source, and work with the teams responsible to eliminate them at a systemic level.
This is a high impact senior program management role within the EMEA Customer Experience organisation, reporting to the Director of Defect Elimination and Customer Experience. The Senior Program Manager is accountable for turning customer experience signals from Wolt and/or Deliveroo markets into clear, actionable insight, and for driving the resulting fixes through to resolution with partner teams.
What you'll be doing
You will own the delivery of the defect elimination program across EMEA, including application of the defect driver taxonomy to identify where defect rate concentrates, and where customer outcomes are worst. You will build a clear, prioritised list of issues for partner teams to work through.
You will represent the voice of the customer in the rooms where decisions get made about your markets. That means preparing and presenting data in product reviews, weekly/monthly business reviews and planning sessions, so the cost of poor customer experience is concrete and attributable, and so partner teams understand what is being asked of them and why.
You will build working relationships with partner teams in engineering, marketplace operations, courier operations, and finance, and you will track the fixes they commit to through to completion. You will feed results back into the program so everyone can see what worked, and to ensure defects are eliminated for good.
You will maintain and improve the data infrastructure and reporting that underpins this work, ensuring customer experience insights are credible, available and actionable.
Our humble expectations
The right person for this role has spent time inside a large-scale customer experience or operations function, and has direct experience translating customer defects through identification, root cause analysis and resolution. They are comfortable working with imperfect data, and they know how to build a credible case when the evidence is directional rather than conclusive.
Strong analytical instincts are essential. This person needs to know what questions to ask of the data and whether the answers make sense. Prior exposure to a successful voice of the customer (VoC) program is critical.
There is a meaningful cross-functional dimension to the role. This person will spend real time getting other teams to prioritise work that benefits the customer but may compete with other priorities. That requires good judgement, clear communication, and the ability to build trust quickly with people outside their reporting line.
The role also requires the ability to drive results in a dynamic and ambiguous landscape. The right person will combine introducing structure and rigor, while being agile and responsive to changing priorities and emerging issues.
This is a high impact and high visibility role, with the opportunity to interact with stakeholders and teams across the full customer lifecycle. The role will also span across 40 EMEA Roo & Wolt markets, meaning there is an opportunity to drive financial and customer experience results at scale.
Next steps
You will first meet with our Talent Acquisition team to understand role and company fit. Then, you will meet with the Hiring Manager who will talk through your relevant experience and ask you competency based questions that assess your suitability for the role.

The third stage is an assignment, where you will be given a business problem to think through, and present back to the team. If successful, there may be a final conversation with a more senior stakeholder. Throughout all stages, you will have plenty of opportunities to ask any questions about the role, team or company.
Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion
We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

A major function of the Office of Data Acquisitions is to provide databases developed from state highway safety related data for use in analyses aimed at reducing deaths, injuries, crashes, and medical costs.

As the Director, the incumbent will be responsible for the following: Advising the Associate Administrator on all matters related to the design, development, coordination, and management of crash investigation and data collection, and their contribution to achieving the mission of NHTSA.

Keeps the Associate Administrator fully informed as to the status of programs and of problems and controversial issues.

Collaborates closely with the Associate Administrator and other top officials of NHTSA to identify the agency's crash research and data needs, to determine techniques and methods by which the office can meet those needs, to estimate the cost and time required to meet the needs, and to determine other implications of changes.

Carrying out personnel management responsibilities for a staff of professional, technical, administrative and clerical support personnel. Makes decisions on work problems presented by subordinate supervisors and key specialists.

Evaluates performance of subordinate supervisors and reviews evaluations made by supervisors of subordinate employee's performance. Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the State Data Reporting Systems Division responsible for the crash record-based data.

Crash record based data includes the Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), a fundamental national data base on traffic safety, Crash Report Sampling System (CRSS), Not-in-Traffic System (NTS) and the State Electronic Data Collection Program (SEDC)., The Division also provides the expertise in sample design and quality control to the other offices in the National Center for Statistics and Analysis, the rest of NHTSA and other offices in DOT.

Establishing policy and provides management oversight of the Crash Investigation Division (CID), provides executive leadership in the planning, design, development, coordination, and management of national networks of motor vehicle traffic crash research and data collection activities.

These include the operation of a national system to conduct detailed investigations of a well-defined selection of motor vehicle crashes currently the Crash Investigation Sampling System (CISS)); and the Special Crash Investigations (SCI) program of special investigations of crashes of particular, interest; and Systems for collecting, supplementing, and coding data from police crash reports to provide special purpose data files.

Maintaining liaison with other Federal agencies, State and local governments, police agencies, hospitals, private safety groups, motor vehicle and equipment manufacturers, crash research and analysis organizations, professional societies, and other groups with an interest in crash investigation and crash data for the purposes are for exchanging crash data and information on crash research technology, encouraging the use of crash data, and cooperating on crash research programs.

The ideal candidate is a data executive and systems expert with a track record of managing federal data collection, automation, and national crash investigation programs.

They possess the strategic and technical skills to lead multi-disciplinary teams while directing the human resource, budgetary, and procurement parameters vital to national highway safety initiatives.

A skilled collaborator, they excel at building partnerships across federal, state, and private sectors including law enforcement, public health, and the automotive industry to secure cooperation and advance data systems.

Furthermore, they bring expertise in data governance, enforcing quality control and data completeness while protecting individual privacy, ensuring the delivery of accurate databases that support national safety research and rulemaking.
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must meet the specialized experience qualifications.

To qualify for the Grade 15, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equal or equivalent to the GS-14, it must include: Experience directing multi-disciplinary professional, technical, and administrative teams while managing the organizational, human resource, and budgetary parameters vital to national highway traffic safety initiatives.

Experience communicating with system managers, rulemaking engineers, researchers, technicians, traffic safety administrators, Governor's Representatives for Highway Safety, State and local officials, national data system program managers and others associated with the application of data as it applies to helping solve complex safety issues.

Experience establishing policy and overseeing large federal data divisions to ensure data completeness, security, and rigorous quality control. Examples include working with executive leadership to plan, develop, and manage large-scale national data collection systems and multi-level crash investigation programs.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Technical Knowledge: Knowledge of federal budgeting to manage large divisional funds, appropriations, large-scale national data architecture, data collection methodologies, complex procurement or contracting mechanisms and systems engineering principles required to build and sustain nationwide databases.

Leadership and Supervision: Management and/or team leader skills, including the ability to direct, manage, and develop a diverse, high-performing human resources workforce of technical and administrative staff.

Communication: Communication, presentation, and negotiation skills, including the ability to secure community support, build strategic intergovernmental alliances, and establish private-sector data-sharing partnerships.

Reasoning: Ability to collaborate across federal, state, and private boundaries to improve data accessibility while balancing competing stakeholder priorities.

For all types of consideration, experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

## Projektleitung Pionierprojekt - Traumapädagogische, familiäre Intensivbetreuung ##
### 30% vorläufig befristet für die Aufbauphase vom 1. Januar bis 31. Dezember 2027. ###
Du möchtest Kindern in hoch belasteten Lebenslagen, für die es bisher kaum passende Wohnformen gibt, einen sicheren Lebensort ermöglichen?
Wirke mit am Aufbau eines neuen, familiären und traumapädagogischen Angebots im Kanton Luzern!
Ausgangslage
Die Fachstelle Kinderbetreuung Luzern und Subito Kriseninterventionen entwickeln im Auftrag des Kantons Luzern ein neues traumapädagogisches, familiäres Intensivbetreuungsangebot.

Das Angebot richtet sich an Kinder, Jugendliche und junge Erwachsene bis maximal 25 Jahre mit stark belastenden Bindungs- und Beziehungserfahrungen sowie herausfordernden Verhaltensweisen, für die bestehende stationäre Wohnformen oder Pflegeverhältnisse nicht ausreichend tragfähig sind.

Ziel ist es, dass die Kinder und Jugendlichen im Zuhause eines Menschen mit Ausbildung im Sozialbereich leben, der diese Aufgabe als Haupterwerb übernimmt und zusätzliche Unterstützung von weiteren Menschen aus dem eigenen sowie professionellen Umfeld erhält.
Die erste Projektphase vom 1. Januar 2027 bis 31. Dezember 2027 dient dazu, die fachlichen und organisatorischen Grundlagen sorgfältig zu entwickeln und die Umsetzung ab 2028 vorzubereiten. Dafür suchen wir eine initiative, verbindende und fachlich starke Persönlichkeit, die Freude daran hat, Neues aufzubauen, Menschen zusammenzubringen und traumapädagogisches Wissen wirksam in die Praxis zu übersetzen.
### Funktion ###
Projektleitung Traumapädagogische, familiäre Intensivbetreuung
### Pensum ###
30 %
### Dauer ###
Vorläufig befristet für die Aufbauphase 01.01.2027 bis 31.12.2027. Es besteht die Option einer Verlängerung bei Abschluss der ersten Projektphase.
### Projektziel ###
Aufbau des neuen Angebots: Erarbeitung von Konzept und Kooperationsgrundlagen, Rekrutierung und Anstellung von Betreuungspersonen, allgemeine Vorbereitung der Leistungserbringung, Zusammenarbeit mit externen Anspruchsgruppen aufbauen
### Arbeitsfeld ###
Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, Traumapädagogik, Pflegekinderwesen, stationäre Intensivbetreuung im familiären Umfeld
Deine Aufgabe
In der Rolle Projektleitung gestaltest du die Aufbauarbeit eines innovativen Angebots mit hoher fachlicher und gesellschaftlicher Bedeutung. Du entwickelst tragfähige Grundlagen, steuerst den Projektprozess, vernetzt zentrale Partnerinnen und Partner und bringst traumapädagogische Expertise so ein, dass ab 2028 ein wirksames, familiäres Intensivbetreuungsangebot starten kann.
Deine Hauptaufgaben konkret
* Aufbau der Projektorganisation mit den beiden Kooperationspartnerinnen Fachstelle Kinderbetreuung und Subito Kriseninterventionen und weiteren relevanten Anspruchsgruppen inkl. Leitung eines Projektteams
* Entwicklung des Konzepts für die traumapädagogische, familiäre Intensivbetreuung unter punktuellem Einbezug externer traumapädagogischer Expertise und in Zusammenarbeit mit den zukünftigen Betreuungspersonen
* Definition der Aufnahme- und Ausschlusskriterien sowie der konkreten Leistungsinhalte
* Erarbeitung einer tragfähigen Lösung für die Tagesstruktur, falls vorübergehend kein Schulplatz vorhanden ist
* Aufbau der Zusammenarbeit mit der Luzerner Psychiatrie und Erarbeitung einer Kooperationsvereinbarung
* Ausarbeitung der Stellenbeschriebe und Rekrutierung des künftigen Betreuungspersonals, gewünscht ist eine frühzeitige Einbindung der hauptbetreuenden Person in die Konzeptentwicklung
* Vorbereitung der Arbeitsverträge und weiterer Anstellungsunterlagen für Betreuungspersonen unter Einbezug juristischer Expertise
* Aufgleisung der fachlichen Unterstützung für die Betreuungspersonen, insbesondere Gruppensupervision
* Bekanntmachung des Projekts bei wichtigen zuweisenden Stellen in Zusammenarbeit mit den Leitungen der beiden Kooperationspartnerinnen
* Entwicklung von Instrumenten für die Auswertung der zweiten Pilotprojektphase sowie einer Struktur für den ausführlichen Zwischenbericht
* Erstellung des Berichts zur ersten Projektphase zuhanden der DISG/KOSEG inklusive Zustellung des Konzepts für das Leistungsangebot
Das bringst du mit
Wir suchen eine reflektierte, mutige und verbindende Persönlichkeit, die Freude und Leidenschaft für innovative Pionierarbeit mitbringt. Besonders relevant für diese Aufgabe sind:
* Ausbildung in Sozialer Arbeit, Sozialpädagogik, Heilpädagogik, Psychologie oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation
* Mehrjährige Erfahrung in der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe, idealerweise im stationären Bereich oder im Pflegekinderwesen
* Fundierte Kenntnisse in Traumapädagogik, Bindungstheorie und traumasensibler Beziehungsgestaltung
* Erfahrung in Projektleitung, Konzeptentwicklung und interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit
* Bereitschaft zu einer gleichwertigen Zusammenarbeit mit unterschiedlichen Anspruchsgruppen und Freude an partizipativen Entscheidungs- und Arbeitsformaten
* Sicherheit und Eigenständigkeit im schriftlichen Arbeiten, in der Berichterstattung, im Umgang mit digitalen Hilfsmitteln und im Aufbau fachlicher Grundlagen
* Hohe Selbständigkeit, eine sehr gute Arbeitsorganisation und Freude daran, aus Ideen konkrete nächste Schritte zu entwickeln
* Kommunikationsstärke, Vernetzungsfähigkeit und die Gabe, unterschiedliche Akteurinnen und Akteure konstruktiv einzubinden
Das bieten wir
* Eine sinnstiftende Projektaufgabe mit grosser fachlicher, gesellschaftlicher und menschlicher Relevanz
* Viel Gestaltungsspielraum und eine hohe fachliche Autonomie beim Aufbau eines neuen kantonalen Pilotangebots
* Zusammenarbeit mit erfahrenen Organisationen und Fachpersonen der Kinder- und Jugendhilfe mit kurzen Entscheidungswegen
* Fachlichen Austausch mit traumapädagogischer Expertise
* Sehr flexible Arbeitsgestaltung im Rahmen des Projektauftrags

* Option auf längerfristige Rolle bei erfolgreicher Pilotphase
Worum es im Angebot geht
Im Zentrum des künftigen Angebots steht eine bewährte Idee aus dem nahen Ausland: Eine sozialpädagogische Fachperson stellt ihr eigenes Zuhause für die längerfristige Betreuung eines Kindes zur Verfügung und wird dafür in einem 100-Prozent-Pensum angestellt.

Sie wird von Menschen aus ihrem persönlichen Umfeld sowie von professionellen Unterstützungspersonen begleitet und entlastet. So entsteht ein tragfähiges Netz rund um das Kind und die betreuende Fachperson. Das Angebot verbindet Kontinuität, verlässliche Beziehungen, Schutz, Partizipation und traumasensible Begleitung.

Kinder und Jugendliche sollen einen äusseren und personalen sicheren Ort erleben, korrigierende Beziehungserfahrungen machen und gemeinsam mit Fachpersonen neue Handlungsroutinen entwickeln können.

At Zurich, our ambition is to put customers at the heart of everything we do and become the insurer of choice by building meaningful relationships that earn customer loyalty over time.
Over the past several years, we have made significant progress in building customer thinking into our strategy, products, services and ways of working. However, there is still more to do to ensure customer perspectives consistently shape decisions across the organisation and become embedded in our everyday mindset and culture. We believe better customer understanding leads to better business decisions.
The Group Customer Office plays a central role in this transformation, partnering with markets and functions around the world to ensure the voice of the customer is heard, understood and acted upon. Through customer, market and brand insights, we help the business better understand changing customer needs, identify opportunities for improvement and make decisions that strengthen customer loyalty, drive growth and create long-term value.
To support this effort, we are looking for a passionate, curious and commercially minded insights professional to join our Customer, Market & Brand Insights team. This role is paramount in translating our data and research into actionable insights that influence business decisions and drive meaningful change.
Working closely with markets, regional stakeholders and senior leaders, you will help evolve and deliver our global brand and experience insights tracking tools to deliver value to the business, ensuring customer understanding influences business decisions and actions.
As we continue to embrace AI and new analytical capabilities, we are also transforming how insight is generated and activated, allowing us to spend less time producing reports and more time influencing decisions and delivering impact.
Reporting to the Head of Global Brand Tracking & NPS, this role will focus on understanding how our brand health created through our products, services and experiences shapes customer perceptions and behaviours, and ensuring those insights are translated into actions that improve customer outcomes and business performance.

s.h: As Senior Insight Manager you will
s.t:
* Champion the voice of the customer, helping embed customer thinking into decision-making across Zurich.
* Generate compelling customer and brand insights that influence to drive business impact
* Oversee Zurich's global retail Brand and Relationship NPS programmes and lead our Commercial Broker study, ensuring high-quality delivery, governance and business value.
* Evolve our insight programmes and measurement approaches to ensure they remain relevant to changing customer and business needs.
* Transform complex data into clear, actionable recommendations and executive-level narratives that drive action.
* Partner with the insights team, markets, agencies and business stakeholders to identify opportunities, solve business challenges and accelerate customer-centred change.
* Connect customer, brand and business data to strengthen understanding of performance drivers and commercial impact.
* Facilitate discussions and workshops that turn insight into tangible business outcomes.
* Work closely with the Tracking Insight Manager and TNPS Expert to maximise the impact, adoption and activation of insights across the organisation.
* Bring external best practice, innovation and emerging AI capabilities into Zurich's insight ecosystem to continuously enhance how we generate and apply insight.
Work location is Zurich with travel potentially required up to 10%

s.h: As Senior Insight Manager, you will bring
s.t:
* A passion for understanding customers and translating customer, market and brand data into meaningful business opportunities and actions.
* Strong storytelling and communication skills, with the ability to distil complex information into clear, compelling narratives that influence decision-making.
* Proven experience activating insights within organisations, driving awareness, engagement and action across diverse stakeholder groups.
* Expertise in leading continuous and ad hoc qualitative and quantitative research programmes, either within an in-house insights function or consultancy environment.
* Strong commercial acumen and the ability to connect customer insights with business performance, growth and loyalty outcomes.
* Experience managing complex global programmes and building effective relationships across markets, functions and cultures.
* Demonstrated ability to influence and engage senior stakeholders, facilitating discussions and workshops that drive alignment and action.
* Curiosity and practical experience applying AI and emerging technologies to enhance insight generation, synthesis and activation.
* Strong analytical skills with experience working with large datasets and statistical tools (e.g. Excel, SPSS), turning data into actionable recommendations.
* Experience bringing together multiple data sources to identify performance drivers and generate deeper business understanding.
* A degree (e.g. in business studies, marketing, research, psychology, behavioural science, customer or change management or a related field), alongside significant experience in customer, market or brand insights.
* Knowledge of the insurance sector is beneficial but not essential; curiosity, commercial thinking and a customer-first mindset are critical.
* Fluent English, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

The Senior Project Manager, Clinical Operations – Full Service is responsible for providing customer-focused leadership in the management and delivery of the operational, financial, and strategic aspects of clinical research projects from proposal development through final deliverables.

This role oversees studies ranging from single-service programs to large-scale, full-service global clinical trials across multiple phases and therapeutic areas.

The Senior Project Manager serves as the primary client contact, leads cross-functional teams, and ensures projects are delivered on time, within budget, and in compliance with quality and regulatory standards.

Project Leadership & Delivery
Independently manage clinical studies from startup through closeout.
Lead the operational and financial execution of Phase II and III clinical trials, including global and multi-protocol studies.

Ensure studies are conducted in accordance with GCP, ICH guidelines, regulatory requirements, and company SOPs.
Oversee project timelines, budgets, resources, risks, and deliverables.
Drive day-to-day study execution and proactively identify and resolve project issues.
Coordinate activities across functional teams and external partners to ensure successful project delivery.
Maintain accountability for project quality, financial performance, and customer satisfaction.
Client & Stakeholder Management
Build and maintain strong relationships with sponsors and key stakeholders.
Lead client meetings and provide regular project updates.
Independently prepare and present project materials for internal and external meetings.
Participate in bid defense meetings and business development activities as the designated Project Manager.
Support client growth opportunities through exceptional project delivery and relationship management.
Financial & Operational Oversight
Manage project budgets, forecasting, and financial performance.
Monitor project progress through timelines, metrics, tracking tools, and reporting systems.
Develop risk mitigation and contingency plans to ensure successful project outcomes.
Ensure inspection readiness, including oversight of Trial Master Files and project documentation.
Prepare project reports for sponsors and senior leadership.
Team Leadership & Mentoring
Lead and motivate cross-functional project teams.
Mentor and support junior Project Managers and Project Support staff.
Facilitate project-specific and therapeutic area training as needed.
Promote collaboration, communication, and accountability across teams.
Minimum Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Medicine, Nursing, Pharmacy, or a related discipline, or equivalent combination of Bachelor’s degree and experience.

Strong hands-on cross-functional project management experience with direct involvement in study execution.
Experience independently managing project budgets, timelines, resources, and client relationships.
Strong knowledge of GCP, ICH Guidelines, regulatory requirements, and the clinical development process.
Excellent communication, presentation, interpersonal, and leadership skills.
Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Willingness to travel up to approximately 25%.

Du bringst komplexe Web-Projekte erfolgreich über die Ziellinie - indem du Ressourcen, Budgets und Kundenwünsche so gekonnt jonglierst, dass man meint, sie würden die Balance halten. 80-100%, Länggasse Bern, ab sofort - oder wann immer-s für dich passt.Was kann ich bewirken?2026 betreuen wir zu viele zu tolle Projekte - dein Einstieg wird deswegen so spannend wie steil: unser Team und die wichtigsten Prozesse kennenlernen (Konzeption, Schätzung, Entwicklung), dich in die Anforderungen eines konkreten Projekts einlesen - und dieses, eng begleitet von uns, auf den Boden bringen.

Schon bald bist du so die primäre Ansprechperson und das Gesicht von Helga gegenüber ausgewählten Kunden. Damit bist du auch ihr Anwalt: Primär kämpfst du für ihre Interessen. Aber du sagst ihnen eben auch, wenn etwas unrealistisch, überdimensioniert oder unterambitioniert ist.

Du kennst die Projekte deiner Kunden auswendig: Wenn sie anrufen, kannst du auch zu technischen Themen Auskunft geben; damit entlastest du auch unsere Entwickelnden.

Kunden haben Wünsche - du nimmst sie entgegen, definierst gemeinsam mit dem Team Lösungen, erläuterst Kunden gegenüber die Kosten, zeigst Alternativen auf, machst Ansagen - und gibst alles, damit diese wahr werden.

Who the Hell ist Helga?Wir stehen am Morgen auf, um die Welt an diesem Tag einen ganz kleinen Schritt nutzerfreundlicher, effizienter und damit besser zu machen. Um am Abend etwas dazugelernt und gemeinsam eine gute Zeit verbracht zu haben.

Das tun wir als (mit dir bald 12-köpfige) Berner Digitalagentur, indem wir Lösungen entwickeln, die uns herausfordern, immer aufs Neue, mit höchsten Ansprüchen an Technologie und Design. Und mit dem Ziel, Nutzende zu begeistern - und Kunden umzuhauen.

Wen sucht ihr?Ganz kurz: Mit deinem Organisations- und Kommunikationstalent bringst du komplexe Web-Projekte erfolgreich über die Ziellinie und machst unsere Kunden langfristig glücklich. Etwas genauer: Zusammen mit unserem Team von Project Managers hältst du unsere zahlreichen Projekte im Griff.

Konkret: Du- erarbeitest zusammen mit dem Team Offerten, planst deine Projekte zeitlich ein und stimmst sie mit den anderen Projektleitenden ab, führst das Projekt-Controlling, stellst sicher, dass unsere Prozesse eingehalten werden und die verschiedenen Teams (Entwickelnde, Konzeption, Design) untereinander abgestimmt sind, kommunizierst Updates transparent und zielgerichtet gegen innen und aussen, bringst im laufenden Projekt die richtigen Leute zusammen, um Probleme und Lösungen gemeinsam zu besprechen und unsere Projekte vorwärts zu bringen, hilfst, unsere Lösungen zu testen, bevor sie an Kunden gehen und unterstützt unsere Kunden bei Fragen oder Anliegen.

Was erwartet ihr von mir?Ganz ehrlich: Bloss die Vereinigung von zwei Widersprüchen. Du bist begeisterungsfähig, ein Menschenmensch - und dabei strukturiert. Technischer HintergrundAuch wenn wir eine unglaublich menschliche Digitalagentur sind: wir brennen für digitale Lösungen. Dahinter stecken Technologien.

Server, Markup, Datenbanken, Content-Management-Systeme - das sagt dir was, da fühlst du dich zuhause. Und wenn nicht, lässt du nicht locker, bis du-s tust. BegeisterungDu liebst, was digitale Lösungen bewirken können. Du willst schnell lernen an täglich wechselnden Herausforderungen. Du bist ambitioniert und blühst auf an hoch gesteckten Zielen.

MenschenDu kannst-s mit Menschen, reisst sie mit und erwischst den richtigen Ton auch in heiklen Situationen. Du weisst, dass ein gutes Team auch Arbeit bedeutet und fühlst dich dafür mitverantwortlich. StrukturAber eben auch: Du arbeitest strukturiert und genau, bist organisiert und magst Zahlen.

Dein Deutsch ist auch ohne AI korrekt; du drückst dich klar aus - und bleibst dabei herzlich. Sind das viel zu hohe Erwartungen? Jap. Sag uns einfach ganz offen, was du davon mitbringst. Und wieso gerade Helga?Du wirst Teil eines 11-köpfigen Teams - bist also keine Nummer, sondern ein Charakter.

Wir sind konsensorientiert, arbeiten auf das gleiche Ziel hin und finden die beste Lösung gemeinsam. Als Unternehmen und Personen entwickeln und bilden wir uns laufend weiter. Du kannst mitreden, deine Arbeit mitgestalten und unsere Zukunft prägen. Ein paar Fakten?

Hier: Zentrale Lage beim Bierhübeli in Bern Eine ordentliche Kasse für Team-Events, welche alle Mitarbeitenden organisieren: Aareböötle, Oktoberfest, Zelten und Kajakfahren im Jura, ein Skitag - wofür immer die Hälfte deiner Peers stimmt Grosse Dachterrasse mit Hängematte, Grill und Alpensicht Aktives Büroleben - und trotzdem die Freiheit, bis zu zwei Tage pro Woche im Home-Office zu arbeiten Viele Pflanzen, Bar, eine anständige Kaffeemaschine und ein Kühlschrank voller Lieblingsgetränke Ein Notebook nach deiner Wahl und Mitsprache bei den Tools und Technologien, die wir verwenden 5 Wochen Ferien und sehr flache Hierarchien Beitrag an deinen öV-Arbeitsweg Zusätzliche arbeitsfreie Zeit bei Alter, Geburt - und für alle einen freien Tag im September Teilweise Prämienübernahme für Krankentaggeld und Unfall Treueprämien, wenn du lang genug bleibst Gleitende Arbeitszeiten Überzeugt!

Senior Program Manager, Data Security & Information Governance
Why We Have This Role
We’re hiring a Senior Program Manager, Data Security & Information Governance to establish, scale, and orchestrate our enterprise Information Governance program. You’ll sit at the intersection of Legal, Data & Technology Operations, and Enterprise Data, bridging the gap between business strategy, legal compliance, data security, and engineering.

Rather than acting as a traditional gatekeeper, you will build and manage our "Data Front Door" to directly address how teams discover data rights, request entitlements, and explore novel data use cases safely and efficiently.
How You’ll Find Success
Governance Framework & Tooling Strategy: Deep fluency in establishing enterprise data governance frameworks, data catalogs, and business glossaries that scale across high-growth SaaS environments.
Operational Enablement: Proven capability to design centralized intake and triage processes ("Data Front Door") that convert complex legal and security constraints into frictionless, self-service internal workflows.
Cross-Functional Alignment: Ability to bridge legal compliance (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA) with technical access controls (RBAC/ABAC, tokenization), working seamlessly alongside engineering, security, and product teams.
Proactive Execution: Takes initiative to define the "how" in ambiguous regulatory or operational spaces, driving cross-functional alignment and resolving data policy conflicts across teams.
Adaptive Curiosity: A drive to stay ahead of evolving data privacy laws, security architectures, and novel AI/ML data use cases to keep our governance models modern and flexible.
How You’ll Grow
Master Enterprise Data Architecture: Expand your expertise across cloud data architectures (Snowflake, Databricks, AWS/GCP) and automated metadata pipelines to build modern, tech-enabled governance structures.
Bridge Legal and Engineering Operations: Deepen your technical competency in access management (Okta, Immuta, Privacera) and data security capabilities, dissolving the divide between legal strategy and technical execution.
Influence Platform Scale: Set the patterns and primitives for data use across a platform serving 18K+ global clients, ensuring data minimization, privacy-by-design, and compliant AI experimentation.
Things You’ll Do
Build the "Data Front Door": Design and manage a centralized intake and triage process for custom data access requests, novel data questions, and complex derivative work inquiries.
Curate the Data Marketplace: Establish a centralized Use Case Repository and Data Marketplace detailing pre-approved data uses, restrictions, and licensing parameters across distinct datasets.
Automate Metadata & Classification: Partner with engineering and security teams to implement automated data classification, lineage tracking, and metadata harvesting.
Translate Policy into Technical Controls: Collaborate with InfoSec to operationalize legal requirements into enforced technical access controls (RBAC/ABAC) and row/column-level security protocols.
Drive Governance Adoption: Measure program success through adoption KPIs, request turnaround times, and governance maturity metrics, delivering self-service documentation and onboarding across the org.

s.t:
5+ years of experience in Data Governance, Data Security, Data Operations, or Information Architecture within a high-growth technology, SaaS, or data-intensive organization.
Deep understanding of data privacy and security frameworks (HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA) and commercial data licensing nuances.
Direct experience setting up, configuring, or administering enterprise data governance & catalog tools (e.g., Collibra, Alation, DataGalaxy, Atlan).
Technical aptitude with cloud data ecosystems (Snowflake, Databricks, AWS/GCP), SQL, and data security mechanisms (hashing, tokenization, differential privacy).

Enablement Over Gatekeeping: We view governance as a business driver. Our goal is to make doing the right thing with data the easiest path for our product, engineering, and business teams.
Cross-Functional Influence: You will sit at the crossroads of Legal, InfoSec, and Platform Engineering, serving as the connective tissue that translates legal policies into automated technical realities.
Built for Scale: As Qualtrics expands its AI and data capabilities, you will build the foundational governance frameworks that ensure our growth remains safe, ethical, and fully compliant.
Why you’ll want to join us: Most design teams are talking about AI; we are the ones building the engine that powers it. If you want to bridge the gap between design and development, thrive in high-autonomy environments, and see your code directly power intelligent experiences for 18K+ global clients, this is the place to be.
